newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says truckers strike will not hurt growth.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says truckers strike will not hurt growth.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said he believed the truckers' strike would have no impact on 1996 economic growth, which he still saw at 1.3 percent in terms of gross domestic product (GDP).
"It is difficult to assess the total impact. But I believe that on balance the strike will have no impact on 1996 growth," Arthuis told parliament.
He put the total costs of measures announced to solve the dispute, including early retirement, for the state at 800 million francs over an unspecified number of years.
He said that the economic results for the third quarter comforted him in believing that the 1997 GDP growth target of 2.3 percent was attainable.

Arthuis said that the state would pay some 60 to 80 million francs per year to accompany a number of measures agreed between employers and unions concerning early retirement at 55 years in exchange for hiring young workers.
The measures will be in place for 20 years.
"When this degressive system will have ended the total costs for the state will be 800 million francs," he said.
